L355@P7: To further differentiate the source of risk, we zoom into the intra-day pricing dynamics
L356@P7: to examine the lead-lag relations between stocks and bonds at higher frequency. Consistent
L357@P7: with the observation that U.S. Treasuries are the source of risk on bond risky days, we
L358@P7: find that movements in UST can positively predict subsequent movements in the S&P 500
L359@P7: (SPX), but not the other way around.4 Our analysis shows that a 1 bps increase in UST
L360@P7: returns positively predicts a 0.15 bps change in SPX returns in the next five minutes, with
L361@P7: a statistically significant t-stat of 2.65. In contrast, a 1 bps increase in SPX returns predicts
L362@P7: only a 0.01 bps movement in UST returns, small in magnitude and with an insignificant
L363@P7: t-stat of 1.63. These findings confirm that the UST market acts as the primary source of
L364@P7: risk on bond risky days, leading the equity market. Outside of the bond risky days, SPX
L365@P7: can negatively predict UST, while UST does not significantly predict SPX. That suggests
L366@P7: that, outside of bond risky days, the equity market is the dominant driver of risk, further
L367@P7: highlighting the distinct risk dynamics present on the bond risky days captured by our
L368@P7: stock-bond correlation measure.
